units.source_text: 从前，一旦成了名人，就担心有损于名人的权威，连练习也回避同人对弈。

en.t: In the past, once someone became a Meijin, he feared damaging the authority of that title, and even avoided playing practice games with his peers.

units.source_text: 名人以六十五岁的高龄下决胜棋，恐怕是前所未有。

en.t: For a Meijin to play a decisive match at the advanced age of sixty-five was probably unprecedented.

units.source_text: 今后大概也不会允许不下棋的名人存在。

en.t: In the future, too, a Meijin who does not play will probably no longer be allowed to exist.

units.source_text: 从各种意义来说，秀哉名人好像是站在新旧时代转折点上的人。

en.t: In many senses, Meijin Shusai seemed to be a man standing at the turning point between the old era and the new.

units.source_text: 他既要受到旧时代对名人精神上的尊崇，也要得到新时代给予名人的物质上的功利，

en.t: He was to receive the spiritual reverence that the old age gave to the Meijin, while also gaining the material advantages that the new age bestowed on the title,

units.source_text: 于是膜拜偶像的心理同破坏偶像的心理交织在一起。

en.t: and so the impulse to worship an idol and the impulse to destroy an idol became intertwined.

units.source_text: 在这样的日子里，名人出于对旧式偶像的怀念，下了这最后一盘棋。

en.t: In such times, out of nostalgia for the old-style idol, the Meijin played this final game.
